name: Passkey on a nearby phone (hybrid)
plain: A computer shows a QR code and your phone approves the passkey sign in.
meaning: Hybrid transport lets a passkey on a phone sign you in on another device. The computer shows a QR code, the phone scans it, and the two devices check they are near each other over Bluetooth before talking through a relay. It works on a browser with no passkey of its own. An unattended cloud browser or agent cannot finish it without a person holding the phone.

web.api: navigator.credentials.get({publicKey}) with hybrid transport chosen in the browser's passkey sheet; transport value 'hybrid'

access.prompt_ui: Browser passkey sheet with QR code, then phone prompt
access.revocation: Delete the passkey on the phone or in the password manager
access.iframe: Same as top level; cross origin frames need a permissions policy where listed
steps: Site starts a passkey sign in
Browser offers 'use a phone' and shows a QR code
Phone scans, checks Bluetooth proximity and asks for biometrics
Phone sends the signed answer to the page

chrome.note: Desktop shows a QR code for a nearby phone

firefox.note: Depends on the OS passkey dialog; check your platform

samsung.note: Phone side depends on the password manager

fields.name: transports
fields.range: includes hybrid when the passkey can be used from a nearby phone

limits.headline: Can sign you in with a passkey on a phone, with no passkey on the computer
limits.user_action: Scan the QR code and approve on the phone
can: Use a passkey that lives on a nearby phone
Sign in on a shared or new computer
Prove you are near the phone, which blocks remote phishing
cannot: Run unattended; a person must hold the phone
Work without Bluetooth on both devices
Let an agent finish the step
Skip the phone's fingerprint or face check
limits.reach_label: One phone approval per sign in
limits.differs: Needs Bluetooth, internet and a phone with a passkey. Firefox depends on the operating system. Cloud browsers and agents stop at the QR code.

story.what_it_is: A QR code on the screen lets your phone vouch for you. The two devices check they are close so a far away attacker cannot use it.

marketing.name: Passkeys
marketing.pitch: Overview of passkeys and the cross device sign in flow.

story.for_you: You scan a QR code with your phone and approve with your face or finger. Nothing is typed. It is the way to use a phone passkey on someone else's computer.
story.for_makers: Do not assume the user is on a device with a passkey. Offer the phone path and an alternative. For agents and cloud browsers plan a human handoff step at the QR code.

use_cases.example: An employee signs in on a shared kiosk using the phone's passkey.
A bank customer signs in on a new laptop by scanning a QR code.
A shopper checks out on a borrowed computer with a phone passkey.
A user opens a work account on a new machine with the phone.
Staff approve admin sign ins on their phone.
An agent team adds a person to approve the QR step in an automated flow.

risks: Needs Bluetooth and a nearby phone

technical_bounds: Needs the phone to be near and awake
QR scanning is a human step
Support varies by browser and OS

legit_uses: Phishing resistant sign in on any computer
Human approval for agent hand offs
abuse: QR code social engineering at kiosks

history.change: Passkeys and cross device sign in in Safari 16
Chrome desktop adds the phone QR code flow
